summary:
UZHAVAN (உழவன்) is a free Tamil and English website that helps Erode district farmers decide which crop to sow next, using NASA satellite data.
A farmer picks their taluk and village from 393 villages across eight taluks. The tool pulls 1991-2020 rainfall and temperature from NASA POWER, soil pH, carbon and texture from ISRIC SoilGrids, and a NASA GIBS vegetation (NDVI) map shown alongside Google Maps.
The Crop Advisor ranks the top three crops with a score out of 100. The score is simple arithmetic combining water fit, soil effect and profit, weighted by three sliders that capture the farmer's own priorities, with penalties for heat and for repeating the same crop family. Because every number can be checked, there is no black box. A Climate Time Machine slider (2026 to 2050) shows how scenario shifts reorder the recommended crops.
Farmers can also type or speak questions to an AI assistant that answers only from their village's data, photograph a crop for a leaf-health check, leave suggestions in a suggestion box, and call the toll-free Kisan Call Centre line. The backend uses SQLite with login, and offline fallbacks keep it working if the internet or AI fails.
details:
UZHAVAN: Every Farmer's Satellite

UZHAVAN (Tamil for "The Farmer") is a free web page, in Tamil and English, that tells a farmer which crop to sow next, why, and whether that choice still holds in 2050. The farmer picks a village and sees its rain, temperature and soil from NASA POWER and ISRIC SoilGrids. Three crops are recommended, each with a score out of 100 split into water fit, soil effect and profit, with every step of the arithmetic on screen. A slider moves the climate from 2026 to 2050 using NASA NEX-GDDP-CMIP6 projections, and the crop cards re-rank. Each crop card also gives a published fertilizer plan and a weed and pest calendar. The farmer can ask questions in Tamil or English and gets answers built only from that village's numbers. It covers 16 places in Erode district, plus Fresno (USA) and Kano (Nigeria).
